# WTF is Git? {.bkrd-color-1}

## WTF is Git?

::: box-1-list
**Git is a version control system.**

It helps us keep track of changes to a variety of different file types in a software development or data analysis project, including:
:::

- code
- project files
- figures
- reports and manuscripts
- other text-based project documents

Think of it as **Track Changes on steroids**.

---

## Why version control?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Without Git**

- `analysis_final.R`
- `analysis_final2.R`
- `analysis_final_really_final.R`
- `analysis_final_SUPER_FINAL.R`
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**With Git**

A project has a **history**.

You can see:

- what changed
- when it changed
- who changed it
- why it changed
- previous versions
:::
:::

---

## "Can't I just keep different files?"

**Sure.**

You can also use:

- Google Drive
- Box
- Dropbox
- other backup systems

. . . 

::: box-1-list
But a bespoke system is usually **your system**.

Git gives collaborators a shared set of conventions for understanding a project that don't depend on reading your mind or hoping for useful metadata.
:::

## Why learn Git now?

Git becomes especially useful when you work with other people.

::: {.incremental}
- You don't have to remember every change yourself.
- Someone else can pick up your project and understand its history.
- You can experiment without destroying a working version.
- You can recover from mistakes.
- Your workflow becomes reproducible and shareable.
:::

. . . 

::: {.callout-tip}
Learning the process now is easier than learning it under deadline pressure.
:::
